title: EdgeLite packaging and consumption playbook
author: Lena Park
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes EdgeLite: a lightweight, opinionated runtime and consumption model designed for developers who need low-latency, low-footprint inference on constrained devices and small edge nodes. EdgeLite is intended as a packaged option for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers who require local inference with predictable economics and incremental feature parity with hosted Redwood API.

Goals and non-goals
------------------
- Goals:
  - Provide a single binary and SDK bundle that enables model-serving at the edge with minimal ops overhead.
  - Offer tiered consumption modes (microbundle, burst, and standby) with transparent unit economics for customers.
  - Maintain graceful fallback to hosted Redwood variants for heavy workloads or degraded local capacity.
- Non-goals:
  - Not intended to match full throughput of Dedicated GPU fleets.
  - Not a replacement for on-prem heavy-duty clusters or the full Private control plane.

Product highlights (what customers get)
-------------------------------------
- EdgeLite runtime: 80–200MB binary with a single-process model shard loader and an optional lightweight proxy for local multi-tenant routing.
- SDKs: Node, Python, and a minimal Rust client for embedded use.
- Consumption modes: microbundle (per-request microcredits), burst-capacity (short prewarm windows billed as bursts), and standby (low-cost keepalive).
- Telemetry: aggregated anonymized telemetry to Redwood Console + local metrics endpoint for Prometheus scraping.
- Security: support for customer-managed KMS integrations and offline signing for package verification.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
1. Control plane (Redwood Private/Dedicated): model catalog, signing keys, entitlements, and consumption accounting.
2. EdgeLite agent: runs on customer node, enforces local entitlements, selects model shard(s), serves requests via local gRPC/HTTP gateway.
3. Local cache + KV store: small LRU-backed key-value cache for KV-caches and prefix reuse.
4. Fallback proxy: routes requests to hosted or dedicated variants based on routing policy and local health.

Design constraints and tradeoffs
-------------------------------
- Memory and binary size constrained to support small ARM x64 instances and Raspberry Pi 4 class hardware.
- Quantized model support assumed (int8/4-bit); full FP16/FP32 is supported only where hardware allows.
- Prefetch vs. prewarm: prefetching model weights on demand minimizes startup cost but increases tail latency; the bundle provides configurable prewarm windows.

Minimum viable feature set (MVP) requirements
--------------------------------------------
Use the following checklist to determine MVP readiness:

1. Runtime and packaging:
   - Single, signed binary per supported platform (linux-x86_64, linux-arm64).
   - Model loader that supports sharded weights and delta updates.
   - Local HTTP/gRPC endpoint with the same request surface shape as Redwood API (subset).
2. Security and compliance:
   - Signed artifacts with offline verification.
   - Integration points for customer KMS and audit log export.
3. Consumption and billing:
   - Microbundle metering: per-inference microcredit counters persisted and periodically synced to control plane.
   - Burst windows with configurable duration and cap.
4. Observability:
   - Local Prometheus metrics with standard naming conventions.
   - Periodic encrypted heartbeats to control plane for health and accounting.
5. Failover:
   - Policy-driven fallback to hosted variants with priority and latency thresholds.

Packaging and distribution
-------------------------
- Published artifacts: signed tar.gz packages and Docker images.
- Channels: stable, beta, and nightly.
- Auto-update policy for pinned deployments: optional; default is manual update for Private customers.

Recommended configuration table
-------------------------------
| Setting                     | Recommended value                     | Notes |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------|-------|
| Default prewarm window      | 20s                                   | Balanced start-up latency vs cost |
| Microbundle unit size       | 0.01 USD equivalent per 1K tokens     | Adjustable by customer tier |
| Burst duration max          | 120s                                  | Billed at burst rate per second |
| Standby heartbeat interval  | 300s                                  | Low-cost keepalive for ephemeral nodes |
| Local cache capacity (MB)   | 256                                   | Adjustable; recommend >=128MB for most cases |

Pricing & packaging notes
-------------------------
- EdgeLite introduces two new priceable primitives: microcredits and burst seconds.
  - Microcredits: purchased in bundles (microbundle) or deducted from tenant credit balance. One microcredit approximates 100 tokens on typical quantized models; conversion and modeling must be displayed in Console before purchase.
  - Burst seconds: short prewarm windows purchased as a metered resource; priced per second of active prewarm across a node pool.
- SKU options:
  - EdgeLite Self-Managed: platform binary + metering; billed per microbundle and optional support fee.
  - EdgeLite Managed: includes managed rollout and auto-updates; adds a monthly node management fee.
- Migration discounts: customers migrating from Dedicated to EdgeLite-managed hybrid setups can receive a credit proportional to reserved capacity for the first 6 months.

Developer experience and onboarding
----------------------------------
1. Quickstart path (self-serve):
   - Install CLI, register node with 'redwood-edge register --org <org-id> --node-name <name>'.
   - Pull a verified model 'redwood-edge pull-model --model redwood-v1-mini --shard 0'.
   - Start runtime 'redwood-edge start --config edge-config.yaml'.
   - Send a test request using SDK until a green health check is observed.
2. Templates: pre-built Helm chart for k8s, systemd unit example, Raspberry Pi distro image.
3. SDK ergonomics: maintain parity in request/response fields with hosted API where feasible; clearly document disabled features in EdgeLite (e.g., no long-running streaming beyond burst window).

Operational runbook (incident triage summary)
-------------------------------------------
- Symptom: Node unresponsive to local requests.
  1. Check local systemd logs: journalctl -u redwood-edge.
  2. Verify disk and memory usage (df -h; free -m).
  3. Check local Prometheus metrics endpoint for model-loader error counts (/metrics).
  4. If certificate or signing errors appear, rotate keys via control plane and restart runtime.
- Symptom: Unexpectedly high microcredit usage.
  1. Use local request logs to identify request patterns and prompt lengths.
  2. If traffic spike expected, consider temporary burst enablement or redirect to hosted fallback.

SLOs and acceptance criteria for GA
-----------------------------------
- Functional SLOs:
  - Model load success rate: >= 99.5% across supported nodes during typical prewarm.
  - Local net-tail latency (95th percentile): <= 250ms for single-turn small responses on ARM64 with small quantized variants.
- Operational SLOs:
  - Heartbeat delivery: >= 99% within a 5-minute window per node.
  - Metering sync: per-node billing sync delay <= 10 minutes for 95% of nodes.

Roadmap and milestones
---------------------
- Phase 0 (Q4 2029): internal alpha; core runtime and microcredit accounting.
- Phase 1 (Q1 2030): beta with Node + Python SDKs and two model families supported.
- Phase 2 (Q2 2030): GA, managed offering, pricing published, Console integration for microbundle purchases.
- Phase 3 (H2 2030): support for on-device hardware accelerators and expanded ARM/embedded platforms.

Dependencies and risks
----------------------
- Dependencies:
  - Lightweight quantized model packaging from model-onboarding team.
  - Metering and billing pipeline extension for high-frequency microcredit events.
  - Legal sign-off on node licensing and export controls.
- Principal risks:
  - Underestimating operational complexity for customers managing many small nodes.
  - Metering reconciliation edge cases causing billing disputes.
  - Security posture for devices in hostile networks.

Acceptance checklist for release to GA
-------------------------------------
- [ ] Signed security review and threat model complete.
- [ ] Billing reconciliation tests with synthetic nodes passing for 100k events.
- [ ] Console UI for microbundle purchasing and visualization implemented.
- [ ] Documentation and quickstarts published across SDKs.
- [ ] Support runbook and escalation paths published to customer-success.

Release notes (initial GA blurb)
-------------------------------
EdgeLite GA (v1.0) — 2030-04-15
- Key highlights:
  - Lightweight runtime and SDKs for local inference on modest edge hardware.
  - New consumption primitives: microbundles and burst seconds with integration into Redwood Console.
  - Transparent fallback policies to hosted Redwood variants.

Appendix: example edge-config.yaml snippet
-----------------------------------------
# Example configuration (YAML)
node_id: "edge-node-42"
model: "redwood-v1-mini"
prewarm_window_seconds: 20
consumption_mode: "microbundle"
microbundle_id: "mb-std-1"
heartbeat_interval_seconds: 300
fallback_policy:
  - condition: "cpu_usage>80% or memory_free<200MB"
    action: "route_to_hosted"
